solutionReview.headline: At $t=0$ the model gives {{A}}: the starting number of cells.
reasoning: At $t=0$, $({{b}})^0=1$, so the model gives ${{A}}({{b}})^0={{A}}\cdot 1={{A}}$ cells.
The {{b}} is the factor applied each time interval; {{A}} is the starting amount.
So {{A}} represents the number of cells at time $t=0$.
solutionReview.commonError: Confusing the starting amount {{A}} with the growth factor {{b}}, or reading the model as adding cells each interval.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The number of cells at time $t=0$

solutionReview.headline: Each month adds one more factor of {{b}}: subscribers are multiplied by {{b}}.
reasoning: When $t$ goes up by 1, the power $({{b}})^t$ gains one more factor of {{b}}.
For example, after 1 month ${{A}}\cdot {{b}}={{s1}}$, and after 2 months ${{A}}({{b}})^2={{s2}}$, which is ${{s1}}\cdot {{b}}$.
The number of subscribers is multiplied by {{b}} each month.
solutionReview.commonError: Reading {{b}} as a number of subscribers added each month: an exponential model multiplies; a linear one adds.
solutionReview.answerSummary: The number of subscribers is multiplied by {{b}} each month.

solutionReview.headline: Compare starting values and growth factors separately.
reasoning: At $x=0$ every power is 1, so the starting values are {{A}} for $f$ and {{C}} for $g$, and ${{A}}>{{C}}$.
The growth factors are the bases, {{b}} for $f$ and {{d}} for $g$, and ${{d}}>{{b}}$.
So $f(0)>g(0)$ and $g$ has the greater growth factor.
solutionReview.commonError: Assuming the function that starts larger also grows faster. The starting value and the growth factor are separate.
solutionReview.answerSummary: $f(0)>g(0)$ and $g$ has the greater growth factor.
